articleBody:
Adding a bathroom brings immediate convenience, but skipping crucial planning steps can turn a high-value upgrade into a headache. Below is a checklist of critical items to verify before work begins.

- [ ] Measure fixture clear floor spaces — Building codes require minimum clearances in front of toilets, sinks, and showers so the room functions comfortably.
- [ ] Confirm building, electrical, and plumbing permits — Unpermitted mechanical rough-ins can halt work during municipal inspections or complicate home resale.
- [ ] Verify drain pipe slope and main stack capacity — Tying new waste lines into existing plumbing requires adequate fall and capacity to prevent recurring clogs.
- [ ] Route exhaust ducting directly to the outside exterior — Venting a bathroom fan into an attic or ceiling cavity traps moisture and triggers mold growth.
- [ ] Specify dedicated electrical circuits for bathroom outlets — High-draw appliances like hair dryers require proper circuit breaker capacity and GFCI protection.
- [ ] Select approved shower waterproofing systems — Water intrusion behind tile damages structural framing and subfloors over time.
- [ ] Finalize vanity, faucet, and shower fixture rough-in dimensions — Plumbing rough-ins must match specific manufacturer cut sheets before closing up walls.
- [ ] Check subfloor integrity and level across the room — Heavy tile installations require a stiff, unyielding base to prevent grout cracking.

How to use this checklist:
Review each item with your project lead during the initial walkthrough. Confirming these details early prevents mid-project surprises, delays, and change orders.
